Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class CapabilityAndPersistenceGameTests

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.CapabilityAndPersistenceGameTests
public final class CapabilityAndPersistenceGameTests extends Object
The automation surface and the saved state behind it: the item handler exposed on every side, a run advertising its reachable headroom, and each type's update tag round-tripping the contents and presentation state it is responsible for.

  • Method Details

    • itemCapabilityIsAvailableFromEverySide

      public static void itemCapabilityIsAvailableFromEverySide(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal Forge lookup check: query all six sides and the unsided capability of each stack type; every lookup must expose item storage.

      To check the sided behavior manually, place each type with one admissible item and attach a compatible transfer machine to each face in turn. Each attachment can access contents. The unsided lookup has no direct player gesture.

    • singleBlockCapabilitiesAdvertiseConfiguredHeadroom

      public static void singleBlockCapabilitiesAdvertiseConfiguredHeadroom(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal Forge slot-count check: single Storage, Singles, and Bar blocks advertise two blocks of slots when maximum height exceeds one, otherwise one. This does not insert or grow.

      Nearest manual check: configure max_pile_height above one, place one block of each type, and use slot-addressing automation to inspect advertised capacity. Repeat with height one. Actual growth is covered by the growth tests.

    • capabilitySimulationDoesNotMutateAnyStack

      public static void capabilitySimulationDoesNotMutateAnyStack(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal Forge simulation check, exercising Singles only: simulate inserting five apples into grounded slot 0. The remainder is four, the offer stays five, and storage stays empty.

      No ordinary player gesture performs a capability simulation. Use a slot-addressing machine or test probe that can simulate without committing; the nearest visible behavior is that a dry-run transfer stores nothing.

    • nativeForgeReloadPublishesPolicy

      public static void nativeForgeReloadPublishesPolicy(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper) throws IOException
      To reproduce: edit render_gallery.gen_mods in the world's somestacks-server.toml while the server runs; /ss gen mod list reflects Forge's reload without restart. The fixture edits the file directly in its own batch and waits for native publication using a wall-clock deadline, since accelerated GameTest ticks do not measure file-watcher latency. File, native value, and common policy are restored on completion or failure. The edit overwrites without truncation to avoid coalescing truncate/write notifications, which NightConfig's watcher skips when their event count exceeds one.
      Throws:
      IOException
